```text
  - **SkillScan HTTP hosts**: recognize HTTP/HTTPS schemes case-insensitively in both URL regexes and prefix checks, without changing source evidence. Use URL authority parsing for lowercase hosts and bracketed IPv6 loopback; userinfo must never hide an external host. Malformed URLs remain outbound for exfiltration checks. Cleartext HTTP detection covers IPv6 literals; cloud-metadata hostname matching is case-insensitive. Coverage: `tests/test_skillscan_native.py`.
  - **Python secret mappings**: `secret-env-assignment` scans literal container values and conditional branches under secret-like bindings. Dictionary keys are structural labels and contribute candidates only when their folded literal matches the shared `_SECRET_TOKEN_PATTERNS`; they must not inherit credential evidence from the enclosing variable name. Opaque keys without a recognized token format stay unreported. Regressions in `tests/test_skillscan_native.py` cover runtime-loaded mappings, nested labels, credential-value locations, and literal/concatenated token keys; `tests/test_skill_review_core.py` pins the CI CLI gate.
> - **Skill Review Core**: `packages/harness/deerflow/skills/review/` provides read-only package snapshots, deterministic facts, resource/eval analysis, report rendering, and the CLI (`python -m deerflow.skills.review.cli`). It reuses the shared frontmatter helper and SkillScan; it must not import `app.*`, execute target scripts, install dependencies, or call networks. JSON contracts live in `contracts/skill_review/`. The analyzer hands SkillScan a byte-faithful copy of every non-symlink snapshot file (binary entries carry `content_base64`), so package rules such as `package-executable-binary` cover binaries; only eval-fixture `SKILL.md` samples are withheld, while scripts and other files under `evals/fixtures/` are scanned. Materialization uses exclusive create, so a duplicate archive member or a case-folded name fails the scan closed (`not_assessed: skillscan`) instead of overwriting an earlier file, as does an entry without bytes in an untruncated snapshot. The `review_skill_package` built-in tool labels results with `review_subject_entry` and never `skill_context_entry`, so reviewing a target does not activate it, bind its `required-secrets`, or apply its `allowed-tools`. Its model-visible `ToolMessage.content` is a compact JSON payload with untrusted control tags neutralized; the full raw review payload, including Markdown renders, stays in `ToolMessage.artifact`. CI should run the CLI with `--fail-on error --fail-on-incomplete` so blocker/error findings and truncated/not-assessed packages fail the gate. The public `skills/public/skill-reviewer` skill owns semantic readiness review and suggestions only; mutation and runtime experiments remain owned by `skill-creator`.

> - **Loading**: `load_skills()` recursively scans public, per-user custom, global integration, and legacy custom locations for `SKILL.md`, parses metadata, and reads enabled state from extensions_config.json plus per-user skill state for non-public categories; that directory is a package boundary, so no nested `SKILL.md` is registered as a runtime skill. A custom skill directory may be a one-level symlink to an external directory for compatibility with operator-managed skill trees; activation still rejects a symlinked `SKILL.md` or deeper path escape. Deleting such a skill unlinks the entry and leaves the external tree untouched. SkillScan has a deliberately narrower packaging rule: known eval fixtures are permitted as support data, while other nested `SKILL.md` files are reported as package defects. Ancestor-link cycles are pruned; independent aliases remain discoverable.
  - **External reload**: `POST /api/skills/reload` is an admin-only, process-local invalidation hook for trusted MinIO/NFS/CSI writes. `SkillStorage` instances do not cache a catalog — `load_skills()` scans on every call — so the route clears all `(app_config, user_id)` entries and the rendered prompt-section LRU, then waits up to the shared refresh timeout for the existing off-loop single-flight refresh. Each invalidation receives a generation-bound result handle; a successful scan atomically replaces the global enabled-skills cache, while a loader-level failure propagates to the HTTP waiter and preserves the last-known-good global cache. Per-user/config scans capture the refresh version and cannot repopulate shared caches if invalidation occurs while they are loading. A timed-out HTTP wait fails generically while the daemon refresh worker continues. Subsequent runs rescan after a successful reload; active runs keep their existing snapshot. Each Uvicorn worker/Kubernetes Pod must be targeted separately. Direct mount writes bypass install/edit validation, SkillScan, and history, so mounted roots are an operator-controlled trust boundary.
  - **Tool policy**: Agent `allowed-tools` declarations apply dynamically only to slash-activated skills and skills captured in `ThreadState.skill_context` through configured `read_file` loads; passive enabled skills and skill allowlists do not clamp the baseline tool set. A lead custom Agent's explicit `skills` list is additionally enforced at the sandbox filesystem layer (see Sandbox projection); subagent skill lists still scope discovery and activation only because concurrently delegated subagents share the lead thread sandbox. Subagents render only skill discovery metadata at startup and reuse the same adjacent `SkillActivationMiddleware` + `SkillToolPolicyMiddleware` pair as the lead; their configured `skills` field limits discovery and activation instead of eagerly loading bodies or unioning policies. Slash policy is dominant for its run, preventing subsequently read skills from widening explicit authority; autonomous captured skills use the existing union only when no slash source exists. `tool_search` and `describe_skill` stay available as framework discovery infrastructure, while every discovered or promoted business tool still requires active-policy permission for schema visibility and execution; `task`, `list_background_tasks`, and `cancel_background_task` likewise require explicit declarations. Each active model call intentionally reloads the full live registry so enable/disable changes, frontmatter edits, and custom/public name-shadow winners take effect without a stale TTL or unsafe direct-path cache; all tool calls produced by that model step reuse the resulting source-and-path-signed decision. Registry failures and all-invalid active sets fail closed, while stale individual paths are skipped when another valid skill remains. The dynamic `allowed-tools` policy remains best-effort behavioral scoping: alternate loading paths are not captured and bounded autonomous context may evict entries.

```text
  - Prefer contract-level tests over implementation details. Avoid asserting internal helper wiring, field assignment, singleton identity, incidental ordering, prompt boilerplate, or passthrough option forwarding unless another component depends on that exact detail.
  - Don't duplicate coverage across abstraction levels. If an integration test already proves the behavior, drop the narrower unit test that restates it through mocks.
> - Tests **must be full-suite safe**, not just file-local safe. No long-lived file-wide mutations of `Bun.*`, `process.platform`, `process.env`, or `Bun.env` when a narrower seam exists. Prefer per-test `vi.spyOn(...)` with `vi.restoreAllMocks()` in `afterEach`. A test that passes alone but poisons later files is broken.
  - **Never use `mock.module()`**. Bun's `mock.module()` mutates the global module registry and leaks across files ([oven-sh/bun#12823](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/12823)). Use `spyOn` on the imported module object instead. For pass deps, import the pass and spy on `.run`. For package deps, namespace-import and spy on the exported function.
  - For lifecycle/stateful code, prefer one test per invariant or transition over several tiny tests asserting one field each from the same transition.
```

**[966]** fixture · root · [AGENTS.md:312](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/b19830726837519349f7df91ea06d563a786413b/AGENTS.md#L312)

```text
  - Assert exact strings, ordering, and formatting only when downstream code parses or depends on the exact bytes. Otherwise assert semantic content.
  - Compile-time guarantees → type checks/type tests, not runtime placeholders.
> - **Never source-grep.** A test that reads an implementation file (`.ts`/`.rs`/build script) and asserts on its _text_ — `expect(src).toContain("someCall()")`, `.toMatch(/import .../)`, `.not.toContain("oldName")`, or "comment must say X" — is banned. It tests how code _looks_, not what it _does_: it breaks on harmless refactors (comment reflow, rename, import reorder) and passes while the behavior is broken. Assert the observable contract instead (run the code, check output/state/error), use the runtime smoke probe for wiring you cannot exercise in-process, and enforce structural invariants (no value-import of X, no self-import) with a type test or an oxlint rule — never a string scan of the source. (Reading a file your code _wrote_ — apply-patch result, generated bundle, temp fixture — and asserting on that output is fine; that is behavior, not a source grep.)
  - Don't add tests for tiny low-risk changes unless they protect a real contract or fix a regression-prone edge case.
  - Prefer focused package-local verification for the changed area.
```

  ## Integration test mechanics
  
> `tests/integration/conftest.py` does several non-obvious things — read it before writing new integration tests:

**[991]** fixture · nested · [backend/CLAUDE.md:93](https://github.com/chirpz-ai/pandaprobe/blob/3be22101411cb9cd467692885586dc91dddbb08c/backend/CLAUDE.md#L93)

```text
  - **`nest_asyncio.apply()`** at import time so Celery's `asyncio.run(...)` works inside the pytest-asyncio loop (eager mode).
  - **TRUNCATE-based isolation**, not transaction rollback. The Celery task creates its own session/connection (matching real worker behaviour), so wrapping each test in a transaction would hide its commits from the test code. After each test, every table is `TRUNCATE ... CASCADE`d and the async engine pool is `dispose()`d so pooled connections don't leak into the next test's event loop.
> - **Fixed seed UUIDs** (`TEST_ORG_ID`, `TEST_PROJECT_ID`) so every fixture in a test shares the same identity.
  - **`autouse` dep overrides** replace `get_db_session`, `require_project`, and `get_redis` for every test. The overridden `require_project` returns a pre-built `ApiContext` — no auth roundtrip.
  - **Redis `FLUSHDB`** runs at the end of every test so rate-limiter counters, eval locks, and usage counters don't bleed across tests.
```

Migrations: hand-authored `NNNN_*.sql` applied in order by the checksum-tracked runner (`packages/db/src/migrate.ts`, tracked in `_app_migrations`); the `packages/db` suite runs `migrate()` against real Postgres. A shipped migration is **immutable**, and the two ways to break that fail differently. **Editing** one (a comment counts) moves its digest and wedges every already-migrated database at that file, which no later migration can repair. **Renaming or deleting** one is invisible to the runner, which keys on name: the file re-applies as new and orphans its old ledger row, silently. Change a shipped migration with a new migration; `no-mutated-applied-migration` enforces this because a fresh-DB suite cannot see either case, and `migrate-immutability.test.ts` pins both behaviours. Numbering is the other half of the same contract: a new migration takes the next unused number, never a hole, a letter suffix, or anything below `0001`, because name order is apply order — `no-backfilled-migration` enforces it from the directory listing, the only oracle that can tell a backfill from a fresh tree. See `docs/contributing/coding-rules.md` "A migration number is never reused and never backfilled".
```

  - Use `toSlash` (also from `pathslash`) only where an **external-origin** string enters the codebase: `process.cwd()`, `config.root`, `fileURLToPath`, `require.resolve`, `fs.realpathSync.native`, node's glob output, and bundler-reported ids (`resolveId` importers, `watchChange`). Everything downstream of a pathslash call needs no normalization.
> - `toSlash` is platform-gated (a no-op on POSIX) — and that IS the contract: Windows-style paths do not occur on POSIX at runtime. Never add an unconditional `.replaceAll("\\", "/")` to source just to make a cross-platform test pass, and don't feed Windows-shaped fixtures to tests that run on every platform. Gate Windows-only scenarios with `it.runIf(process.platform === "win32")` and keep their assertions unconditional (see `tests/build-optimization.test.ts`, `tests/dev-stack-sourcemap.test.ts`). `tests/app-route-graph.test.ts`'s `vi.mock("pathslash", ...)` (win32 flavor) is the one deliberate exception, kept so POSIX CI exercises the route graph's Windows semantics.
  - Do NOT write "must be forward-slash" JSDoc contracts — the import itself is the guarantee.
  - Do NOT touch URL-space backslash defenses (request-pathname `replaceAll("\\", "/")` sanitizers) — those are URL hygiene, not filesystem paths.
```

## 205. cocoindex-io/cocoindex-code

python · 1 fixture match · root

**[1048]** fixture · root · [CLAUDE.md:68](https://github.com/cocoindex-io/cocoindex-code/blob/b883be0b5d762c9e2d7d82afdedeade5df21d5be/CLAUDE.md#L68)

```text
  `find_project_root()` walks up from CWD looking for `.cocoindex_code/settings.yml`. Global settings at `~/.cocoindex_code/global_settings.yml` (location overridable via `COCOINDEX_CODE_DIR`). The `COCOINDEX_CODE_DB_PATH_MAPPING` env var redirects database files to a different directory (used in Docker to avoid LMDB on bind mounts).
  
> `ccc index` and the legacy `cocoindex-code` entry point never auto-create project settings in the directory whose `.cocoindex_code` *is* the user settings dir (`is_user_settings_root()`: `$HOME` by default, `/x` for `COCOINDEX_CODE_DIR=/x/.cocoindex_code`), and the hooks and OMP extension never index it. With the documented Docker mount (`$HOME:/workspace`, `COCOINDEX_CODE_DIR=/workspace/.cocoindex_code`), `/workspace` is that directory. An explicit `ccc init` there is still allowed, for deliberate whole-tree indexing and single-repo mounts such as the Docker e2e fixture. `ccc reset` there removes only project files, never `global_settings.yml` or daemon files.
  
  
```

```text
  - **Socket path:** Unix uses `<version-dir>/daemon.sock` and keeps the short hashed `tmpdir()` fallback when the natural path reaches 100 characters. Windows binds the pipe digest to the canonical version directory plus the current user discriminator; request authentication remains the security boundary.
  - **OpenCode bootstrap:** dist/bootstrap resolves the package `./cli` export instead of deep-running generated files. Source mode runs the actual `src/cli.ts` with Bun and sets the paired `OMO_LSP_DAEMON_CLI`/`OMO_LSP_DAEMON_VERSION` override to that source CLI plus the package version. The OpenCode adapter supplies only the three `LSP_TOOLS_MCP_*` translator inputs for request context: `.opencode/lsp.json`, `.omo/lsp.json`, `.omo/lsp-client.json`, then the OpenCode user config and install-decision paths.
> - **Legacy cleanup input:** `test/fixtures/legacy-path-vectors.json` freezes the pre-migration natural Unix, hashed Unix, and Windows named-pipe paths for the installer cleanup work. Do not regenerate those paths from the new resolver.
  - **Clean builds:** `scripts/clean-dist.mjs` removes the complete old `dist` tree before TypeScript and Bun emit new artifacts, so deleted generated files cannot survive a build.
  - **Spawn is detached + log-redirected:** child runs `node cli.js daemon` with `stdio: ["ignore", logFd, logFd]` (→ `daemon.log`) and `unref()`, so the parent session never blocks on it. On Windows every detached/background spawn sets `windowsHide: true` (daemon spawn, version reaper) so periodic helpers never flash a conhost window. The launcher preserves `process.execPath` while it exists, falls back to an existing absolute `process.argv0`, then to PATH-resolved `node`; spawn errors are recorded in the log instead of escaping as an uncaught child-process event.
```

Nothing starts until the tool is activated: a `tool_activated` event naming `computer` opens the engine session and arms the stop chord. Settings come from the omo `computer` block, snake_case and native-only, mapped onto desktop-tool's resolver. Per run it composes (never clobbers) a sentinel-delimited compiled memory block through `before_agent_start`, committed-HEAD-only and cached by (template, HEAD). Registers two sequential tools (`memory`, `memory_apply_patch` with letta-exact semantics incl. first-occurrence `str_replace` and clean-check->commit; excluded from senpi-task children via `uiOnlyToolNames`), ten slash commands (`/memory /memfs /remember /init /doctor /recompile /memory-repository /sleeptime /reflect /search`), a self-contained palace HTML viewer (0600/0700, machine-gated), a `tool_call` soft cross-identity guard plus a registered filesystem policy when the host exposes `registerFilesystemPolicy`, memfs skill scope via `resources_discover`, and a journal/debug status line with an advisory at `compile_warn_tokens` (30000). ```text
  - Don't skip tests due to type issues - fix the types instead
  - Test both success and failure cases with edge cases
> - Keep added tests as minimal and dense as possible without sacrificing comprehensiveness; avoid redundant assertions or broad fixtures when a focused case proves the behavior.
  - No log statements (`console.log`, `debugger`) in tests or production code
  - Never stack prose across consecutive `//` lines. Lines have no maximum width here — the editor wraps for display — so a paragraph split across several `//` lines is just a hard-wrapped line, and hard wrapping breaks search, diffs and editing. Write one long `//` instead. `nub run check:comments` enforces this in pre-commit and CI; `--fix` joins the offenders. Commented-out code, `@ts-`/`@__NO_SIDE_EFFECTS__`-style pragmas, bullet lists, and blocks separated by a bare `//` are exempt. When two adjacent comments describe two different statements, separate them with a blank line rather than joining them.
```

  - **Forwarded headers** (own source, `REQUEST_HANDLING_ROOTS`: every app + auth, server-functions, ee, jobs, lib, utils, edge functions): `noRawForwardedHeaders` fails a raw read of `X-Forwarded-For/-Host/-Proto` or `X-Real-IP` outside `packages/utils/src/headers.ts` — use `getClientIp` / `getRequestProtocol` / `getRequestHost` / `getRequestOrigin`. Hand-rolled reads keyed login rate limits and ITAR audit records on the forgeable first `X-Forwarded-For` entry. No baseline entries
  - **Error log messages** (same source as forwarded headers, `REQUEST_HANDLING_ROOTS`): `noInterpolatedErrorLog` fails `logger.error(`…${value}`)` / `.fatal` — the message is exported as a span attribute and is what errors group by, so values are named (`"Failed to upload {fileName}", { fileName }`). One baseline entry: the `packages/auth/src/utils/result.ts` pass-through, whose message is its caller's
> - **Numeric-precision checks** (in `TS_CHECKS`, over `sources/typescript.ts`): `noRawRounding` flags `Math.round/ceil/floor` and `.toFixed` on value-bearing numbers (use `round`/`scrapAllowance`/`applyRate`/`deriveRate` from `@carbon/utils`); `noInlineFractionDigits` flags `minimum`/`maximumFractionDigits` at a call site (pick a named kind from `@carbon/utils` `format.ts`, and `INPUT_FORMAT.*` for anything editable); `noUnroundedTrackedQuantity` flags inline unrounded arithmetic inside a `.updateTable("trackedEntity")` statement's `quantity:` set, and a raw `===`/`!==`/`<` compare against a `*[Ee]ntity*.quantity` read (use `round`/`settleQuantity` at the write, `isFullDraw` at a split gate — see `.claude/rules/traceability-model.md`). It is scoped to what one file can prove: a `quantity:` set from an already-rounded variable is unflaggable either way, and a compare of two locals is presumed rounded where they were defined. It has **no baseline entries** — the whole tree was fixed in the pass that added it, so any finding is new. `sources/typescript.ts` walks `apps/erp/app/{components,hooks,modules,routes}`, `apps/mes/app`, `packages/database/supabase/functions`, `packages/database/src`, `packages/{server-functions,ee,jobs}/src`, `packages/documents/src/{pdf,utils}` and the shared packages `packages/{utils,files,form,react,printing}/src` — tests (`*.test.ts(x)`, `*.spec.ts(x)`) and `*-test-fixture.ts` live-database fixtures excluded; a fixture is test support code, so it is held to the tests' rules, not shipped code's. The shared packages matter: `@carbon/utils` is where the standard's own helpers live, and `form`/`react` own the number inputs whose `formatOptions` are part of the storage round-trip. See `.claude/rules/numeric-precision.md`
  - **Realtime** (in `TS_CHECKS`): `noPostgresChanges` fails a `postgres_changes` subscription — the `supabase_realtime` publication is empty, so it would never fire. Use a broadcast topic through `@carbon/query` (`.claude/rules/realtime-system.md`).
  - **Missing audit columns** (built in `collectFindings`, not `TS_CHECKS`): `noMissingAuditColumn(columns)` fails a write that names `createdBy`/`updatedBy` on a relation that has no such column — PostgREST rejects the whole statement (`PGRST204 Could not find the 'createdBy' column of '<table>'`) and TypeScript does not flag it, because supabase-js widens the insert/upsert argument enough for the excess property to survive. That is how the `customerPartToItem` upsert in `sales-rfq.$rfqId.map-lines.ts` shipped with an unchecked result, so every RFQ-line → customer-part mapping silently failed. Roughly a third of Carbon's tables have no audit columns (favourites, link tables, the lean material lookups, `companySettings`) while golden rule 3 says to include them, so it is an easy assumption to carry into the wrong table. It takes the column map as an ARGUMENT — `loadDbTableColumns(root)` (`sources/db-columns.ts`) reads the generated `packages/database/src/types.ts` `Row:` blocks, so the I/O stays in `sources/` and `scan` stays pure, the same shape as `noAuthzDdlInMigrations(loadManagedFunctions(root))`. Scope is the LITERAL argument of the write (`.from`/`insertInto`/`updateTable` + `.insert`/`.upsert`/`.update`/`.values`/`.set`); a payload object spread into the row is invisible here, and for the MCP/API layer that same generated schema drives `withoutAbsentAuditColumns` in `scripts/lib/service-metadata.ts`. No baseline entries — the one hit was fixed when it was added

```text
  - **Edge-function auth** (`EDGE_FUNCTION_CHECKS`): `edgeFunctionAuthorizesCaller` fails any function under `packages/database/supabase/functions/` that never calls `requireCaller` / `requireServiceRole` — the gates each self-contained function defines for itself; a declaration alone does not count — because `verify_jwt` accepts the published anon key
  - **Server-function shape** (`SERVER_FN_CHECKS`): `serverFnAuthorizesCaller` (`server-fn-authorizes-caller`) fails any `packages/server-functions/src/<name>/index.ts` not built with `defineServerFn`, whose required `permissions` field declares what the caller needs.
> - **License headers** (own source, `sources/license-files.ts`: git-tracked `.ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx/.mjs/.cjs/.rs` under `apps`, `packages`, `crates`, `docs`, `ci`, `scripts` and the repo root): `spdxLicenseHeader` fails a file whose first lines are not its SPDX header — `AGPL-3.0-only`, or `LicenseRef-Carbon-Commercial` under `packages/ee/` and for any `.ee.` file name. The header text, the classification, the exclusions (each with its reason: generated files a generator would clobber — `generate:types`, `generate:swagger`, the workflow catalog, `sst-env.d.ts`, the notification preview fixtures — and third-party copies) and the insertion rules live in ONE module, `src/license-headers.ts`, shared with the fixer `pnpm --filter @carbon/checks license-headers` (`--check`, `--dry-run`, `--verbose`, optional paths; root alias `pnpm license:headers`), so the check fails exactly the files the fixer would change. The header goes after a shebang and above everything else (`"use client"`, `// @ts-nocheck`, `/// <reference>`, `biome-ignore-all`, `deno-lint-ignore-file`, Rust `//!`/`#![…]` all stay valid after a comment), then one blank line; the other license's header is swapped, CRLF is kept. A file with a third-party notice (foreign SPDX id, `@license`, copyright) is flagged and never rewritten — add it to `PATH_EXCLUSIONS`. When the header wording changes, move the old lines to `RETIRED_HEADER_LINES`. No baseline entries
  - **Structure checks**: `moduleShape` — validates ERP modules have `types.ts`, `ui/`, `index.ts`, `<name>.service.ts`, `<name>.models.ts`

  - **Type guards over `as`** — Narrow with a type guard, an `asserts` function or an `in` check rather than an `as` assertion, and explain any assertion that remains with a "Safe because" comment. See [Type Assertions](./guides/typescript.md#type-assertions).

**[1185]** fixture · root · [CLAUDE.md:456](https://github.com/cyrusagents/cyrus/blob/8e786086b21c8dbbc72683830508517b99a62f05/CLAUDE.md#L456)

```text
  9. **Adding a new top-level `EdgeWorkerConfig` field**: Adding a property to the `EdgeConfigSchema` Zod schema in `packages/core/src/config-schemas.ts` is **not enough** to make it available at runtime. Two hand-maintained copy sites exist, and both now have guardrails that fail fast when a field is missed (added after `strictMcpConfig` was silently dropped in CYPACK-1478; `slackAllowedTools` & friends were dropped the same way in CYHOST-967):
  
> - **Cold start** — `WorkerService.startEdgeWorker()` in `apps/cli/src/services/WorkerService.ts` spreads the entire file config (`...edgeConfig`) into the `EdgeWorkerConfig`, so plain pass-through fields flow automatically and need **no** code change. Only add an explicit line below the spread if the field needs env-var precedence or a computed/param override — never add a redundant pass-through line. The `"forwards every EdgeConfig field"` test in `WorkerService.test.ts` has a schema-complete fixture that fails when a new schema field isn't covered.
  - **Hot reload** — `ConfigManager` in `packages/edge-worker/src/ConfigManager.ts` merges a hardcoded list of fields in `loadConfigSafely()` and watches the same list in `detectGlobalConfigChanges()`. Both are driven by the `RELOAD_MERGED_KEYS` const at the top of the file, which has a **compile-time exhaustiveness check**: adding a schema field without classifying it into `RELOAD_MERGED_KEYS` (plus a merge line in `loadConfigSafely()`) or `RELOAD_EXEMPT_KEYS` is a `tsc` error that names the missing key.
  
```

  `next-env.d.ts` (gitignored) is what makes tsc resolve the ambient `.svg`/`.css` module declarations in `lib/utils/types.d.ts` — it's listed first in `tsconfig.json`'s `include`, and tsc needs that entry to exist for the rest of `include` to take effect. A byte-fresh clone has no `next-env.d.ts` (`next dev`/`next build` normally generate it), so `ensure:typegen` backfills it with `next typegen` — a route-type generation step, not a full build — before `typecheck`/`check` run. `next-env.d.ts` also imports `.next/types/routes.d.ts` and `.next/types/root-params.d.ts`, and the post-checkout hook deletes `.next/types` on every branch switch, so `ensure:typegen` checks all three files and regenerates when any is missing. It's a no-op once they exist, so `bun run check` is order-independent: run it before or after `bun run build`, doesn't matter.
  
> Route smoke coverage is automatic: `e2e/route-sweep.e2e.ts` discovers every `app/**/page.tsx` at test-collection time and runs the five-assertion smoke against it with only static segments; dynamic routes (`[slug]`, `[...slug]`) need a bespoke `*.e2e.ts` with fixtures — creating the page is the only step for a static route. Write a bespoke `*.e2e.ts` only for behavior beyond the smoke (see `e2e/not-found.e2e.ts` for the soft-404 example).
  
  When verifying behavior that depends on env vars being _absent_ (e.g. an integration's unconfigured fallback), wipe `.next` before building: `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values are inlined at build time, so hiding `.env.local` against a stale build still renders the configured page and your verification silently measures the wrong variant.
```

  **Release presentation and credits (owner-set 2026-09-17):** Tagged release announcements lead with the biggest user-visible change; redesigns need real UI screenshots and migrations need installer links and steps. Verify all contributor credits from the tag comparison and included PRs; list authors and bug reporters separately (see `docs/RELEASING.md`). Keep Highlights to 3–5 bullets; the release introduction can include prose, images, and a download table before the concise change entries.
  
> **Localization (hard rule):** No hardcoded non-English (CJK) **user-facing text** anywhere in the codebase except the translation layers: `electron/src/renderer/src/i18n/` (the catalog the app loads; checked by `tests/test_locale_parity.py` and Electron `locale:check`) and the legacy `electron/src/shared/i18n/` (loaded only by shared-module tests). All UI strings go through i18n (`t('...')` keys in `locales/*.json`); native language names live in `i18n/index.ts` (`LANGUAGES`). Functional CJK is allowed and tracked via the allowlist in `tests/test_no_hardcoded_cjk.py` — text-processing regexes, model/engine vocabulary & identifiers (e.g. CosyVoice speaker IDs), localized error matching, demo/eval data, and test fixtures. CI fails on any hardcoded CJK outside the allowlist; to add legitimate functional CJK, extend `_ALLOWED_FILES` there with a justification.
  
  **Release deployment channels (hard rule, owner-set 2026-07-16):** a version bump is not "released" until **every** maintained channel ships it — the full checklist lives in `docs/RELEASING.md`. The channels are the Electron GitHub Release (Linux x64, Windows x64 + experimental ARM64, macOS arm64 + x64), GHCR and Docker Hub in CUDA and ROCm flavors, and the Docker Hub overview page synced from `deploy/dockerhub-overview.md`. The final Tauri feeds are immutable compatibility assets copied into releases for old clients; they are never rebuilt. Verify all channels after tagging. Preview/RC builds always source from `main`; never cut a side-branch build.

  **Perf regressions are caught by the scaling test, not the absolute-time ones** — `tests/v2/test_benchmark.py::test_parse_cost_grows_no_worse_than_linearly` times a repeated unit at n vs 4n over a table of shapes (one per pipeline inner loop) and bounds the ratio; the `_thousand_names` tests use constant-size, delimiter-free input and are structurally blind to a complexity regression. Two rules when touching it: calibrate `_MAX_RATIO` against the WEAKEST quadratic's signal (a mixed quadratic surfaces far below the textbook 16×, so the operating point `_BASE` matters more than the bound), and confirm a planted regression fails it across REPEATED runs — one failure is a coin-flip on a timing test. The shapes cover different dimensions (segment count only via `commas`, intra-piece accumulation only via `particles`/`conjunctions`, non-ASCII input only via `honorifics` — every other unit is pure ASCII, so `script_segment` returns at its bail and the CJK stages go unmeasured, M2's clause view only via `maiden_clause`, the one unit holding a marker (until #601 its order mattered, `MA nee ` reaching nothing; since #601 either order reaches the take) — and connective RUN LENGTH only via `link_run`, whose unit has to be MIXED CASE and hold a connective of the generational class: `i und ` reads the letter as an initial and reaches nothing where `i Und ` reaches everything, and S2's anchor pass only via `credential_run`, whose unit has to hold a Title-case member behind an unambiguous credential: `PhD MA ` reads the same fields and never asks the pass, the capitals deciding each member first); measure before pruning one. **A shape whose input needs a PREFIX cannot be a `_SHAPES` row at all**, since that table repeats a unit and nothing else — a maiden clause needs a name word and a marker before the run it is about, and `"nee i Und " * n` reaches the clause rule not at all, measuring the identical ratio on a broken tree and a fixed one. That one is `test_a_clause_link_run_does_not_cost_quadratically`, which builds its own input and counts FRAMES. A prefixed shape whose cost is Python-level joins `_REREAD_SHAPES` beside it — (input builder, the one function the defect re-runs, reachability probe) rows counted in that function's frames at 8 units against 32 — which holds #558's trailing fixed point, its maiden-clause twin, and #559's particle chain, a shape that grows at both ends and so has no unit to repeat. A prefixed shape whose cost is C-level work — a list scanned by `in`, a tuple re-hashed as a dict key — emits no frame for that count to see, so it goes in `_PREFIXED_SHAPES` instead: (prefix, unit, reachability probe) rows timed on the clock like `_SHAPES`, at a base of their own recorded beside the table (#553, whose run shape read 5.97× once at base 800 on the pre-fix tree, under the bound; py3.11, 2026-09-28). **That table skips under a line tracer** (`sys.settrace`, coverage's core below py3.14), which slows every Python line and not the C-level scan, diluting the quadratic below the bound (5.46–5.52× broken at base 1600 under `coverage run` on py3.11, same date). The `sys.monitoring` core coverage uses from 3.14 does not dilute it (8.87–10.91× broken), and CI collects coverage in its 3.14 build job alone, so every CI job runs the table; `ja-extra` also sets `NAMEPARSER_REQUIRE_CLOCK_GUARDS` so that a line tracer there fails the rows instead of skipping them. **Coverage is collected on ONE interpreter, the one that uploads it** (`COVERAGE_ON` in `.github/workflows/python-package.yml`): the package has no version-conditional code, so one report stands for all of them, and under a line tracer the property grids in `tests/v2/test_properties.py` had cost the 3.12 job most of its ~12 minutes (measured 2026-09-29: the three #397 grids take 139s under coverage's settrace core on 3.12, 24s under its sys.monitoring core, 17s with none). **A shape the CLOCK cannot reach needs a FRAME-count guard instead**, which is the second scaling test in that file (`test_a_trailing_credential_run_does_not_cost_exponentially`, #531): where the defect is an exponential rather than a quadratic, the input length that separates the curves on a timing test does not finish, so the guard counts frames over 8 units against 16 and bounds THAT ratio. One pair does not see every curve, and the fix round for #531 measured why: at 2× the input the per-member LINEAR work swamps a quadratic (2.08× for a genuine one against 1.73× clean), so that pair guards the exponential alone and a second, longer pair — 16 against 64, where the same quadratic reads 7.42× against 3.53× clean — is what can see one. Assert them in that order: an exponential never returns from the longer run, so the cheap pair has to have failed first. **A frame guard counts ONE function, so it goes blind when the code it watches stops calling that function.** #563's paired-initials guard counted `_normalize`, which segment's scan reached; #613 moved the scan into `_comma.decide`, where it calls `is_suffix_piece`, and the quadratic came back while the guard read 3.6× and passed (review caught it: 120 → 1,620 calls for 4× the input). When code under a frame guard moves, re-take the guard's negative control on the moved code before trusting a pass. Frame counts do not move under load, so this shape needs no repeated-run calibration — but it does need the same reachability assertion `_POLICY_SHAPES` rows carry, since the walk under measurement runs only while every unit still reads as a credential. A stage gated on an opt-in `Policy` field needs a `_POLICY_SHAPES` entry instead, since bare `parse()` never enters it — and that table's rows carry a **reachability probe** run before the measurement, because a precedence change can quietly stop the shape reaching the stage and leave a green test measuring a no-op (`_POLICY_SHAPES` is also asserted non-empty: an empty `parametrize` is a skip, not a failure, so deleting its last row would retire the guard silently).
  
> **Expected-failure tests use `@pytest.mark.xfail`** — the conftest parametrized fixture breaks `@unittest.expectedFailure`; always use `@pytest.mark.xfail` instead.
  
  **`lc()` strips leading and trailing periods** — `'M.D.'` → `'m.d'`, not `'md'` (interior periods are preserved). Shipped keys in `capitalization_exceptions` are dot-free, so lookups must also try `.replace('.', '')`; whatever key matches, its value is a case mask applied to the word as written, never substituted for it (#459).
```

```text
  - **Unreadable files** (not JSON, or neither `doc` nor `canvas` at the top) open read-only and `getViewData` returns the file text, so a merge conflict or a cut-off sync is never replaced by an empty diagram. `readonly` still lets viewport actions through, which is why the text, not `editor.value`, is handed back.
  - **`isPlaintext` is false**: with the default, an outside change during an unsaved edit is merged into the JSON as text. False takes the file's version and drops the unsaved edit.
> - **The schema GC runs after a load**, so a document that is inconsistent (FK flags with no relationship, for one) can change without an edit. The smoke fixture is kept consistent for that reason.
  - **`styles.css` overrides `contain: strict !important`** on diagram leaves only. Layout or paint containment makes the leaf the box `position: fixed` resolves against, and the editor places its menus with viewport coordinates, so they landed offset by the leaf's position.
  - **The editor's shortcuts reach it while its tab is active.** Obsidian's keymap listens for `keydown` on the window in the capture phase, and a key that matches a command's hotkey goes to that command and is prevented and stopped before the page sees it, whether or not the command applies there. `Alt+Enter` (add column) is Follow link under cursor, `$mod+K` (search) Insert Markdown link and `$mod+F` (Find and Replace) Search current file, and a hotkey the user sets can take any other shortcut. The workspace asks the active leaf's `view.scope` first (Obsidian's own canvas view keeps its keys the same way), `Scope.handleKey` answers with the first matching registration's result, and the keymap prevents the key only when that is `false`.
```

**[1309]** fixtures · nested · [packages/app/AGENTS.md:68](https://github.com/dineug/erd-editor/blob/ec72112ba09b87bdbe1a7337bdbd4b9c3710daa8/packages/app/AGENTS.md#L68)

```text
  - **SQL, DBML, AML and GraphQL are converted before their schema is stored**: the app has no parser, so `convertSource` creates an `<erd-editor>` it never attaches, calls `setSchemaSQL` / `DBML` / `AML` / `GraphQL` with `{ placement: 'auto' }` and reads `value` once the Promise it returns settles (the owner's call on 2026-10-04). Two tables or more with a relationship are stored placed by Flow, on the editor's ELK worker, as an import from the editor's own menu lands (`packages/erd-editor/AGENTS.md`); anything else, a failed layout and a browser without `SharedWorker` store the grid. The element is never attached, so the toast a slow layout raises and its Cancel never show, and a layout waits for the worker or its deadline, which stores the grid. Every caller waits the same: the list's import, the sample and a `/gdrive` import (`driveImport.ts`'s default `convert`) convert their sources one after another, and the notice comes after the last (`import-export.spec.ts` and `gdrive-files.spec.ts` check the placement). Connector anchors and relationship flags follow from hooks milliseconds after the document lands, so the stored value lacks them until the first open derives them, which the fingerprint leaves out and so saves without an `updateAt` (a `service.test.ts` case and `import-export.spec.ts` pin it). The element starts as a new document and the import keeps its settings, so a converted source is stored as a new document too, every lock on (`lockSettings` 63, `ignoreSaveSettings` 3): opening and zooming it stores the derived anchors with the zoom still 1, which `import-export.spec.ts` checks. The element is destroyed in a `finally`, once the placement has settled. The module is imported on demand, since it brings in the whole editor. A source it throws or rejects on counts as an invalid file.
  - **An import stores everything in one `importSchemaEntities` call** and opens the last document or source, unless the selection changed while it ran. `.erd` / `.vuerd` / editor `.json` are stored as they are, but only in a shape the editor recognises (`isEditorDocument`: version `3.0.0` with `doc`, or v2 with `canvas` and `table`), since its parser takes any object as an empty schema. Source extensions are an own-key `Map` lookup.
> - **An import reads no file over 64 MB** (`MAX_IMPORT_FILE_SIZE`) and says so in the notice. A document takes about 600 bytes a column (the `data/` fixtures), so 1,000 tables are some 14 MB and a backup of several fits; `file.text()` of a larger stray file risks the tab.
  - **File drops are taken only when `dataTransfer.types` includes `Files`** (`useFileDrop.ts`); the editor's own drags of tables and columns carry none and must keep passing through.
  - **Files import one import at a time, and the controls show it** (the owner's call on 2026-10-04, after `/gdrive`'s `importing`, which disables its sidebar's Import files). From the start of `useImportFiles` to its notice, `importingFilesAtom` disables the sidebar's Import files and turns the empty viewer's into Radix's `loading` spinner, and a file drag shows Importing files… with `dropEffect` `none`; `useImportFiles` refuses files given meanwhile, as `/gdrive`'s session does, so files dropped then are neither imported nor queued. `/gdrive`'s empty viewer spins its Import files on `importing` too; that route takes no drops. The sample keeps its own spinner and marks nothing. `import-export.spec.ts` and `gdrive-files.spec.ts` hold the `convertSource` module (`support/conversion.ts`) to watch the state come and go.
```

  - `agent-hub.test.ts` prints one `[agent-hub e2e] vscode <version> <spec>:` line per timed spec, `one peer` (join, applyActions, applyToDirty, save) and `two peers` (applyToOtherPeer); applyToDirty is the replica round trip that `join` and `save` wait on, about 210–225 ms on 1.138.0, against their 500 ms and 2 s caps.
```

  - **Assert on what gets sent, not that something was sent.** For an output module, parse the body that was passed to the mocked transport (`json.loads(call.kwargs["data"])`, `kafka.send.call_args.args[1]`, `bucket.put_object.call_args.kwargs["Key"]`) and verify the *fields and values a dashboard or downstream consumer would actually filter on*. A test that only checks `mock.assert_called_once()` would pass even if the payload were `{}`.
  - **No trivial passthrough tests.** A test that calls a getter and asserts it returns the value just set isn't testing the code; it's testing Python's attribute machinery.
> - **A test named for an exclusive claim must observe both halves of it.** "Only", "never", and "exactly once" each assert a negative as well as a positive; when the shared fixture can't observe the negative half (the folder already exists, the cache is already warm), build a fresh fixture for it rather than substituting an adjacent always-true assertion (#863: the "`Unsaved` folder created *only* with a callback" test asserted an unrelated folder existed in place of the untestable without-callback half).
  - **No `# pragma: no cover`.** If a branch is unreachable, the right fix is to delete the branch, not to hide it.
  
```

```text
  - **Moved code** (#849: a "verbatim extraction" carried a latent handler-dedup asymmetry past review, and had just gained a new caller that widened its exposure). A "pure move" is a claim about behavior preservation, not an exemption from review — read extractions cold, and be *more* suspicious when a hunk gains callers than when it changes logic.
  - **Extracted helpers** (#849: a promoted helper lacked the bound check its old call site had made unnecessary, and its docstring misdescribed its stop path). A helper inherits none of its call site's implicit guarantees: it needs its own eager input validation and docstring↔behavior check even when every current caller is safe.
> - **Fixes made during review** (#851: fixing `__getstate__` and stopping there left `__setstate__`'s version-skew hole — old pickles into new code — unexamined; `__init__` never runs during unpickling, so missing fields end up not defaulted but *unset*). Touching one direction of a paired protocol (`__getstate__`↔`__setstate__`, save↔load, encode↔decode) obligates re-deriving the inverse, including inputs no current fixture produces. The review isn't done when the fixes are written.
  - **Rewritten code, for coverage** (#858: a log-equivalent rewrite of the disposal loop shipped its error handler uncovered). Rewritten lines are new patch lines even when behavior is intentionally identical.
  - **Mid-incident glue** (#834: hand-written bootstrap code duplicated the script's existing `wait_for()` helper). Firefighting is not an exemption: before writing new shell/infra code mid-incident, check the file for an existing helper that already does it, and give your own inline code the same scrutiny you'd give a subagent's.
```

  ## Local dev secrets
  
> If a config file is listed in `.gitignore`, treat its contents as secret. Do not paste its literal values into any tracked file — READMEs, docs, code comments, commit messages, PR descriptions, sample/test fixtures. Reference the variable name (e.g. `$SOME_PASSWORD`) or show a placeholder (`...`) instead, and tell the reader to pick their own values. This is both a real-leak hedge and a way to keep secret scanners (GitHub secret scanning, push protection, third-party scanners) from firing false positives on the repo. Defer to `.gitignore` as the source of truth on what's secret — the rule applies to any gitignored config file the project ever adds, not just the ones present today (currently `.env` and `parsedmarc*.ini`).
  
  ## Editing tracked data files

```text
  - **Count enumerations against the code-defined set they enumerate** — derive the set from the code and count both sides; a reader can't tell an intentional subset from an omission (#851: docs listed seven of the eight `config=`-accepting functions).
  - **A quantified claim is an enumeration in disguise, and "pre-existing" triage stops applying when the diff extends its set** (#858: the `config=` paragraph's "arguments listed above are ignored" was filed as pre-existing looseness — but the PR added four arguments to the list that claim quantifies over, making it false for them).
> - **Build verification fixtures containing what the sample corpus lacks** — optional fields, injected errors, over-the-cap sizes — because an absent field makes the wrong key and the right key behave identically (#839).
  - **A contract that signals failure two ways owes both ways the same safety bookkeeping.** When a callback can report failure by sentinel return *and* by raising, grep for every raiser and trace it through the same retention/cleanup logic as the return path — and remember that propagation claims range over every backend the code runs under (#863: `fail_on_output_error` made the save callback raise instead of returning `False`, skipping the retry-cap bookkeeping, while the IMAP and Maildir watch loops swallow exceptions — so "propagates out of the watch loop" was true for two of four mailbox backends and the cap silently never applied on the others).
  - **Bookkeeping paired with a side effect must follow it, not precede it.** Clear or advance tracking state only after the operation it tracks succeeds, and trace each failure branch of that operation for what prematurely-cleared state means (#863: the retry counter was popped when a message was classified over-cap, *before* the move to `Unsaved` was attempted; a failed move handed the still-in-place message a fresh set of retries — survived the implementer and two fresh-context reviews).
```

```text
  - `test_cards.py`, `test_dashboard.py`, `test_keepalive_status.py`: dashboard/card hydration and service status checks.
  - `test_cli_contracts.py`, `test_form_and_helper_source_contracts.py`, `test_frontend_contracts.py`: CLI, form/helper, and DOM/template/view contract coverage.
> - `test_jobs.py`, `test_job_cancel.py`, `test_vm_sync_now_view.py`: job queueing, cancellation, and targeted VM sync behavior. `test_jobs.py` also owns the sync-job **preflight** behavior tests — that a confirmed-empty backend or a missing/unusable FastAPI backend blocks the run before any stage, that an ambiguous or already-populated backend does not, that a NetBox with **zero enabled `NetBoxEndpoint` rows** blocks unconditionally — with stale rows deliberately present on the backend, and the test asserting `list_backend_netbox_endpoints()` is never even called — that **zero enabled `ProxmoxEndpoint` rows** produce a fail-loud `endpoint-scope` record instead of an unscoped all-backend stage request (again with stale backend rows present, asserting the SSE transport is never reached), that the happy path emits no hint (a spurious one would misattribute unrelated stage failures), that the selected `fastapi_endpoint_id` reaches both the context resolver and key registration (with two enabled backends, checking the wrong one fails a working sync), that endpoint-scope failures fail the job with a message distinguishing "No sync stage ran" from "N Proxmox endpoint(s) were skipped", that an unresolvable endpoint whose every selected stage is sync-mode-disabled is recorded as a *skip* rather than failing the job, that the selected backend pk reaches all four pre-SSE service passes (cluster/node, firewall, datacenter, VM templates), and that `PreflightResult` does not share a mutable default. Three tests cover the push budget: `PREFLIGHT_ENDPOINT_PUSH_BUDGET` cuts the loop short while still emitting a warning phase per skipped endpoint, the budget **never** skips an endpoint the backend does not already hold (skipping it would leave it without a wire id and fail the job outright), and `PREFLIGHT_ENDPOINT_PUSH_HARD_CEILING` skips even unregistered endpoints. Those tests drive a fake `time.monotonic` from the push stub itself rather than sleeping. A fourth budget test, `test_preflight_budget_never_skips_an_endpoint_whose_credentials_rotated`, pins the Proxmox credential fingerprint (migration 0074) at the job level: with every backend row held and current on the wire, an endpoint whose secret rotated after its fingerprint was recorded — and one whose fingerprint was never recorded — are both pushed despite an exhausted budget, because `ProxmoxEndpointPublic` withholds the credential fields and only the local receipt can tell a no-op refresh from a push that delivers a new secret (`_arrange_slow_push` records the held rows' fingerprints through the **real** helper for exactly this reason). The recording end has its own Proxmox twins — `test_recording_a_pushed_proxmox_fingerprint_updates_the_row_without_saving_it` and `…_survives_an_unapplied_migration` — mirroring the NetBox pair (write through `queryset.update()`, never `save()`; a missing 0074 column degrades to always-push instead of failing the push), plus `test_proxmox_and_netbox_credential_fingerprints_never_compare_equal`, which feeds both fingerprint functions identical material and pins that the distinct salts keep the two namespaces disjoint. `test_run_scopes_firewall_and_datacenter_to_the_runs_endpoints` pins that `run()` forwards `endpoint_ids_to_sync` to the firewall and datacenter passes, which used to build their own all-enabled scope and ignore the job's selection. Two attribution tests pin `proxmox_endpoint_credentials_rotated_since_last_push()`: a failed Proxmox push over credentials rotated since the last successful push names the rotation in the warning and the carried-forward hint (proxbox-api still holds the previous secret, so the endpoint's reads will fail to authenticate until a push succeeds) while staying non-fatal — and a never-vouched endpoint (no recorded fingerprint, the normal fresh state) does **not** get that claim, so the message stays meaningful on the runs where a rotation really happened. They also share `_preflight_proxmox_endpoint(pk)` / `_arrange_slow_push(..., held=…)`, which build **complete, current** backend rows rather than bare `{"name": …}` stubs — `backend_holds_proxmox_endpoint()` now means "held *and* current", so a row missing `port`/`username`/`access_methods`/`verify_ssl` reads as drifted and the budget correctly refuses to skip it, which is not the behavior those three tests are about. A further group pins the **backend-pin round trip** that keeps a *replayed* job on the same proxbox-api: `enqueue()` persists `fastapi_endpoint_id` into `job.data['proxbox_sync']['params']` (coercing `"7"` → `7` and dropping an unusable value entirely rather than storing a half-parsed pk), still forwards the kwarg to `run()`, omits the key when unpinned, and `proxbox_sync_params_from_job()` reads it back on **both** return paths — including the legacy targeted-VM name inference, which rebuilds the params from scratch. `_coerce_fastapi_endpoint_id` is parametrized directly, `True`/`False` included (a `bool` is an `int` in Python and must not become endpoint 1). Two further tests pin that the coercion happens **before** `super().enqueue()` and **again** at the top of `run()`, which is what keeps the queued RQ kwargs and `job.data` from disagreeing: `test_enqueue_never_queues_a_pin_it_refused_to_store` asserts an unusable pin appears in *neither*, and `test_run_recoerces_an_unusable_backend_pin_before_any_lookup` asserts `run()` normalises it before the preflight sees it (direct callers, and RQ payloads queued by a release predating the `enqueue()` coercion, still hand it a raw value). `True` is the sharp case both ways — it survives every guard and Django resolves `pk=True` against primary key 1. A further group pins that **a stored backend row is only trusted once it is identified**: a failed push plus a row whose **resolved connection target** — `(domain or ip_address)` plus `port` — equals this NetBox's warns "may be stale" and continues, while a row with the *same name* but a different target, the right host on a different port, a *different* domain sharing our configured IP, a blank domain at our IP while we declare one, a row reporting no port at all, or nothing but the synthetic `127.0.0.1` push fallback all block with "do not point at this NetBox". Matching by name would pass the first — the backend NetBox endpoint is a singleton updated by position and its payload name is free text. **That positional singleton is itself asserted**: `test_preflight_blocks_when_only_a_later_backend_row_is_ours` feeds a two-row listing whose *second* row is ours and pins that the run blocks anyway, with no "may … stale" warning, because a match at index 1 vouches for a row proxbox-api is not dialling while the stale row at index 0 drives the sync. `test_preflight_continues_when_backend_already_holds_an_endpoint` therefore feeds the *single* row it always claimed to. Two tests deliberately feed the *same* stored row to opposite verdicts: reached-by-address blocks a domain-configured NetBox and continues an IP-only one, because which field the backend dials is what decides identity. Two more pin fix N, that **"unknown" must not read as "ours"**: a failed push whose backend listing *also* failed blocks, unless some other enabled row pushed successfully (that push already wrote this NetBox's credentials into the singleton, so the unreadable listing has nothing left to add). **These tests call the real `backend_holds_netbox_endpoint()` / `backend_holds_proxmox_endpoint()`, installed on the fixture's fake module by `load_real_backend_sync()` — never a hand-written mirror.** That is not a style preference. The fixture used to re-implement the predicate "faithfully", and when the real helper was found to match two different domain-only NetBoxes against each other through the loopback fallback, every test still passed, because they were asserting against the copy. The defect survived six adversarial review rounds that way. `load_real_backend_sync()` path-loads `views/backend_sync.py` once against throwaway stubs (saving and restoring the eight `sys.modules` entries in a `try/finally`) and takes only the pure predicates; everything that performs HTTP is stubbed separately, so nothing there can reach the network. `test_backend_holds_netbox_endpoint_identity_contract` then states the contract directly as a 21-case table against that same real function, in five groups — positive identification, the loopback trap, a different resolved connection target, the port, and the fail-closed inputs — because the `run()`-level tests only exercise one verdict each. The fail-closed group is where the **positional singleton** is pinned: a single junk entry is `False` without raising, and *any* listing longer than one row is `False` too — including two of **our own** rows, and junk followed by ours — because the push overwrites entry `[0]` and entry `[0]` is what the backend dials, so a longer list means nothing in the response says which row wins. The table is what pins the two directions a field-by-field comparison gets wrong: a stored row blank on `domain` at our IP, or naming *another* domain at our IP, must **not** match (both dial a different service at that address), while our own row whose stored IP has since drifted **must** still match, because a row with a domain never dials its address at all. Its rows are built by `_stored_row()`, which supplies a *current* `verify_ssl`/`token_version` by default, because identity and **currency** are separate questions and that table is only asking the first one. `test_backend_holds_netbox_endpoint_currency_contract` asks the second as its own 10-case table: a `verify_ssl` or `token_version` that drifted in **either** direction is refused, whitespace-only differences are not, an *absent* `verify_ssl` or `token_version` reads as drifted (a `False` here blocks the run, so unknown must fail closed), and **currency is only ever asked of the row the backend dials** — a current duplicate sitting *behind* a drifted row does not rescue it, and neither does a current row belonging to a *different* NetBox, both now twice over since a listing longer than the positional singleton is refused before currency is asked at all. Three preflight-level tests take it end to end — a superseded TLS posture, a superseded token scheme, and a row omitting a mandatory trust field all block the run rather than warning and continuing. Four more pin the **secret** the currency check structurally cannot see, because `NetBoxEndpointResponse` withholds `token`/`token_key`: `test_preflight_blocks_when_the_stored_row_predates_an_in_place_token_rotation` (identity says "ours" and currency says "current", both correctly — and the run would still proceed on a revoked token, so the locally recorded fingerprint of the last **successful** push is the only thing left that can tell), `test_preflight_blocks_when_no_push_ever_recorded_a_credential_fingerprint` (an *empty* fingerprint reads as drifted, because unknown must fail closed; one successful push clears it permanently), and two on the writer itself — `test_recording_a_pushed_fingerprint_updates_the_row_without_saving_it` asserts it goes through `type(endpoint).objects.filter(pk=pk).update(...)` and **never** `save()`, since `NetBoxEndpoint`'s `post_save` handler re-pushes to the backend and saving from inside a push would recurse, while `test_recording_a_pushed_fingerprint_survives_an_unapplied_migration` feeds it the `ProgrammingError` an install without migration `0073` raises and asserts the push still succeeds with the fingerprint left empty (i.e. fail-closed, not fail-loud). `_arrange_preflight(..., netbox_fingerprint="current"|"stale"|"absent")` selects the three states, computing `"current"`/`"stale"` through the **real** `netbox_endpoint_credential_fingerprint()` rather than a literal — `salted_hmac` is implemented faithfully in `tests/django_stubs.py` for exactly this reason, since stubbing it to a constant would make every fingerprint compare equal and silently delete the test. Four more pin the **selected-object batch path**: it blocks with zero enabled `NetBoxEndpoint` rows and never calls `_run_batch_selected_sync` (it used to return *before* the preflight entirely), it forwards the job's `fastapi_endpoint_id` into that call, `_run_batch_selected_sync` itself passes the id to every per-object `sync_individual_with_dependencies`, and — via `_arrange_batch_storage_sync()`, shared by the last two so both assert the **whole** call dict rather than one key — it passes `netbox_branch_schema_id` as a keyword and not only inside `query_params`. That last one is not cosmetic: `_sync_dependency()` rebuilds its params from `_CONTEXT_KEYS`, which omits the branch key, so a query-param-only schema id would write the selected object to the branch and every dependency resolved off it to **main**. Those two drive `sync_stages` directly, so they need the `proxbox_sync_job_module` fixture for the `netbox.*` stubs **and** `monkeypatch.setitem` stubs for `virtualization`, `virtualization.models`, `netbox_proxbox.models`, and `netbox_proxbox.services.individual_sync` — `_run_batch_selected_sync` resolves all four lazily, at call time, so `conftest.py`'s module-level stubs do not apply. Four further tests pin that the batch path also resolves the **Proxmox** scope, which fails in the opposite direction from the branch schema: `_run_batch_selected_sync` forwards `proxmox_wire_endpoint_ids` to dependency syncs as both a query param and an argument, the full `run()` asserts the resolved scope (`"1"`) reaches `_run_batch_selected_sync`, and — the two the review round mandated — a run with **no enabled Proxmox endpoint** and a run whose enabled endpoints **resolve to no backend id** both raise `ProxboxPreflightError` with `batch_calls == []`, i.e. proxbox-api is never called. Both use `_arrange_blocked_batch()`, which deliberately leaves *stale* rows on the backend listing: those rows are exactly what makes an unscoped request dangerous, so the run must stop anyway. `test_batch_wire_endpoint_scope_narrows_rather_than_failing_on_partial_drift` pins the design decision that one drifted endpoint narrows the scope (`("11", ["2"], None, {"1": "11"})`) instead of failing the run. Five further tests pin the **per-object pinning** that narrowing alone does not give you, all built on `_arrange_batch_duplicate_identifier_sync()`: two `ProxmoxStorage` rows that are *indistinguishable to proxbox-api* — both `local-lvm` on a `cluster01` — differing only in `cluster_id`, so the two requests they produce are byte-identical apart from the endpoint scope. That is the whole point: Proxmox identifiers are unique per endpoint, not across the estate, so with the job-wide scope both endpoints can answer and one row silently gets the other estate's storage. The five cover each branch of the **four-state** owner resolution — both objects pinned to their **own** wire id rather than the job-wide `"11,22"`; an object whose owner resolves but is **absent** from the map refused with status `424` and *no* backend call appended to `calls`; an object with no reflected `ProxmoxCluster` read as *unknown* and falling back to the job scope **only where that scope names one endpoint** (`"11"`, the first-ever-sync case, which refusing would make unsyncable forever — and where falling back and pinning are the same request, so nothing is being guessed); the *same* unknown object across a **two**-endpoint scope refused with `424` saying the run "spans 2 Proxmox endpoints", since there the fallback is a guess made with identifiers that are unique only per endpoint, and its error names the single-endpoint retry that makes it recoverable; and a cluster claimed by **two** endpoints — *ambiguous*, which is **not** the same state as unknown — refused with `424` naming every claimant, because two endpoints reflecting one cluster is proof the duplicated namespace exists in this estate, so widening back to the job-wide scope would ask both and keep whichever answered (the exact defect being fixed) while picking one would be a guess about where the object lives. Collapsing ambiguous into unknown restores that widening, and the ambiguity test is what fails when someone does. `_proxmox_cluster_objects()` stubs the `.filter(…).exclude(…).values_list(…).distinct()` chain `_owner_endpoint_pks_by_cluster_id()` issues. `test_batch_selected_sync_fails_the_job_when_selected_objects_failed` pins the enclosing consequence: a `batch_result["failed"] > 0` raises rather than finishing **completed**, since every object in a selected-object run was named by an operator and there is no "partial success" reading of a list somebody typed out — and the per-object `424` refusals above would otherwise be visible only in `job.data`. It asserts both orderings that make the failure useful: `job.data` is saved *before* the raise (so the failed row still carries the per-object status and error) and the raise happens *before* the branch merge, with branching deliberately **enabled** so "the merge did not run" is an assertion about ordering rather than about branching being off. A separate 8-case parametrized table pins `_batch_object_core_cluster_id()` — that all five batch types converge on a core `virtualization.Cluster` id, that a backup prefers its *storage's* cluster (the one its own sync params are built from) while a snapshot prefers its VM's, and that an unresolvable object or unknown type returns `None` rather than guessing. **Patch `effective_sync_modes_for_endpoint` on both `jobs` and `jobs.sync_stages`** — `jobs._sync_stage_settings()` re-copies jobs.py's own reference onto `sync_stages` on every run, silently reverting a patch applied to only one of them.
  - `test_preflight_diagnosis.py`: regression suite for netbox-proxbox issue #624 — a fresh install whose sync died on stage `devices` with an opaque `Error ensuring Proxbox tag`. Pins the three behaviors that turn that into a diagnosable failure: `list_backend_netbox_endpoints()`'s three-way `(rows, None)` / `(None, error)` contract, the named readiness budgets in `services/backend_auth.py` plus one-shot authentication budgets in `services/backend_key_adoption.py`, and `_is_retryable_stage_failure()` plus `preflight_hint` attribution in `sync_stages.py`. Reads both modules' constants with `ast.literal_eval` rather than importing the Django-backed authentication module and asserts the adoption state machine's bootstrap-status, authenticated-key-list, and register-key call sites use named constants via an AST walk, so a future inline literal cannot silently reintroduce a too-tight budget. `TestRetryableStageFailure` additionally pins the two marker-matching mistakes the classifier must not make: a **false positive** (HTTP 400 `"timeout must be between 1 and 300"` is a validation rejection, not a transport failure — which is why no bare single-word marker may be added) and a **false negative** (a transport cause nested in a FastAPI `detail` **list** must still retry), plus the invariant that the echoed `input` field is never scanned and that cyclic/over-deep payloads terminate on `_CAUSE_RECURSION_LIMIT`. `test_real_transport_failure_texts_are_matched` parametrizes the *verbatim* strings the transport layer emits (nginx's hyphenated `504 Gateway Time-out` body, urllib3's `HTTPConnectionPool … Read timed out`, `[Errno 111] Connection refused`, httpx's `Server disconnected without sending a response.`, glibc `EAI_AGAIN`/`EAI_NONAME` and BSD resolver errors, and an `ssl` `EOF occurred in violation of protocol`) so a marker can never be reduced to a shape that matches only the paraphrase — four of those eight were genuine misses before this test existed.
  - `test_stage_failure_cause.py`: behavior coverage for issue #383's retry-history diagnosis. It proves every failed attempt is recorded with typed attribution data, the first application failure wins over later transport noise in either order, all-transport failures use the final attempt, identical details preserve the legacy single-line message, divergent details are bounded, non-retryable failures remain byte-compatible, the final error log matches the raised message, and the `init_ok` readiness diagnosis still fires.

Three tests cover the push budget: `PREFLIGHT_ENDPOINT_PUSH_BUDGET` cuts the loop short while still emitting a warning phase per skipped endpoint, the budget **never** skips an endpoint the backend does not already hold (skipping it would leave it without a wire id and fail the job outright), and `PREFLIGHT_ENDPOINT_PUSH_HARD_CEILING` skips even unregistered endpoints. Those tests drive a fake `time.monotonic` from the push stub itself rather than sleeping. The recording end has its own Proxmox twins — `test_recording_a_pushed_proxmox_fingerprint_updates_the_row_without_saving_it` and `…_survives_an_unapplied_migration` — mirroring the NetBox pair (write through `queryset.update()`, never `save()`; a missing 0074 column degrades to always-push instead of failing the push), plus `test_proxmox_and_netbox_credential_fingerprints_never_compare_equal`, which feeds both fingerprint functions identical material and pins that the distinct salts keep the two namespaces disjoint. `test_run_scopes_firewall_and_datacenter_to_the_runs_endpoints` pins that `run()` forwards `endpoint_ids_to_sync` to the firewall and datacenter passes, which used to build their own all-enabled scope and ignore the job's selection. They also share `_preflight_proxmox_endpoint(pk)` / `_arrange_slow_push(..., held=…)`, which build **complete, current** backend rows rather than bare `{"name": …}` stubs — `backend_holds_proxmox_endpoint()` now means "held *and* current", so a row missing `port`/`username`/`access_methods`/`verify_ssl` reads as drifted and the budget correctly refuses to skip it, which is not the behavior those three tests are about. Those two drive `sync_stages` directly, so they need the `proxbox_sync_job_module` fixture for the `netbox.*` stubs **and** `monkeypatch.setitem` stubs for `virtualization`, `virtualization.models`, `netbox_proxbox.models`, and `netbox_proxbox.services.individual_sync` — `_run_batch_selected_sync` resolves all four lazily, at call time, so `conftest.py`'s module-level stubs do not apply. Four further tests pin that the batch path also resolves the **Proxmox** scope, which fails in the opposite direction from the branch schema: `_run_batch_selected_sync` forwards `proxmox_wire_endpoint_ids` to dependency syncs as both a query param and an argument, the full `run()` asserts the resolved scope (`"1"`) reaches `_run_batch_selected_sync`, and — the two the review round mandated — a run with **no enabled Proxmox endpoint** and a run whose enabled endpoints **resolve to no backend id** both raise `ProxboxPreflightError` with `batch_calls == []`, i.e. proxbox-api is never called. Both use `_arrange_blocked_batch()`, which deliberately leaves *stale* rows on the backend listing: those rows are exactly what makes an unscoped request dangerous, so the run must stop anyway. `test_batch_wire_endpoint_scope_narrows_rather_than_failing_on_partial_drift` pins the design decision that one drifted endpoint narrows the scope (`("11", ["2"], None, {"1": "11"})`) instead of failing the run. Five further tests pin the **per-object pinning** that narrowing alone does not give you, all built on `_arrange_batch_duplicate_identifier_sync()`: two `ProxmoxStorage` rows that are *indistinguishable to proxbox-api* — both `local-lvm` on a `cluster01` — differing only in `cluster_id`, so the two requests they produce are byte-identical apart from the endpoint scope. That is the whole point: Proxmox identifiers are unique per endpoint, not across the estate, so with the job-wide scope both endpoints can answer and one row silently gets the other estate's storage. The five cover each branch of the **four-state** owner resolution — both objects pinned to their **own** wire id rather than the job-wide `"11,22"`; an object whose owner resolves but is **absent** from the map refused with status `424` and *no* backend call appended to `calls`; an object with no reflected `ProxmoxCluster` read as *unknown* and falling back to the job scope **only where that scope names one endpoint** (`"11"`, the first-ever-sync case, which refusing would make unsyncable forever — and where falling back and pinning are the same request, so nothing is being guessed); the *same* unknown object across a **two**-endpoint scope refused with `424` saying the run "spans 2 Proxmox endpoints", since there the fallback is a guess made with identifiers that are unique only per endpoint, and its error names the single-endpoint retry that makes it recoverable; and a cluster claimed by **two** endpoints — *ambiguous*, which is **not** the same state as unknown — refused with `424` naming every claimant, because two endpoints reflecting one cluster is proof the duplicated namespace exists in this estate, so widening back to the job-wide scope would ask both and keep whichever answered (the exact defect being fixed) while picking one would be a guess about where the object lives. Collapsing ambiguous into unknown restores that widening, and the ambiguity test is what fails when someone does. `_proxmox_cluster_objects()` stubs the `.filter(…).exclude(…).values_list(…).distinct()` chain `_owner_endpoint_pks_by_cluster_id()` issues. `test_batch_selected_sync_fails_the_job_when_selected_objects_failed` pins the enclosing consequence: a `batch_result["failed"] > 0` raises rather than finishing **completed**, since every object in a selected-object run was named by an operator and there is no "partial success" reading of a list somebody typed out — and the per-object `424` refusals above would otherwise be visible only in `job.data`. It asserts both orderings that make the failure useful: `job.data` is saved *before* the raise (so the failed row still carries the per-object status and error) and the raise happens *before* the branch merge, with branching deliberately **enabled** so "the merge did not run" is an assertion about ordering rather than about branching being off. A separate 8-case parametrized table pins `_batch_object_core_cluster_id()` — that all five batch types converge on a core `virtualization.Cluster` id, that a backup prefers its *storage's* cluster (the one its own sync params are built from) while a snapshot prefers its VM's, and that an unresolvable object or unknown type returns `None` rather than guessing. **Patch `effective_sync_modes_for_endpoint` on both `jobs` and `jobs.sync_stages`** — `jobs._sync_stage_settings()` re-copies jobs.py's own reference onto `sync_stages` on every run, silently reverting a patch applied to only one of them.
  - `test_preflight_diagnosis.py`: regression suite for netbox-proxbox issue #624 — a fresh install whose sync died on stage `devices` with an opaque `Error ensuring Proxbox tag`. Pins the three behaviors that turn that into a diagnosable failure: `list_backend_netbox_endpoints()`'s three-way `(rows, None)` / `(None, error)` contract, the named readiness budgets in `services/backend_auth.py` plus one-shot authentication budgets in `services/backend_key_adoption.py`, and `_is_retryable_stage_failure()` plus `preflight_hint` attribution in `sync_stages.py`. Reads both modules' constants with `ast.literal_eval` rather than importing the Django-backed authentication module and asserts the adoption state machine's bootstrap-status, authenticated-key-list, and register-key call sites use named constants via an AST walk, so a future inline literal cannot silently reintroduce a too-tight budget. `TestRetryableStageFailure` additionally pins the two marker-matching mistakes the classifier must not make: a **false positive** (HTTP 400 `"timeout must be between 1 and 300"` is a validation rejection, not a transport failure — which is why no bare single-word marker may be added) and a **false negative** (a transport cause nested in a FastAPI `detail` **list** must still retry), plus the invariant that the echoed `input` field is never scanned and that cyclic/over-deep payloads terminate on `_CAUSE_RECURSION_LIMIT`. `test_real_transport_failure_texts_are_matched` parametrizes the *verbatim* strings the transport layer emits (nginx's hyphenated `504 Gateway Time-out` body, urllib3's `HTTPConnectionPool … Read timed out`, `[Errno 111] Connection refused`, httpx's `Server disconnected without sending a response.`, glibc `EAI_AGAIN`/`EAI_NONAME` and BSD resolver errors, and an `ssl` `EOF occurred in violation of protocol`) so a marker can never be reduced to a shape that matches only the paraphrase — four of those eight were genuine misses before this test existed.
  - `test_stage_failure_cause.py`: behavior coverage for issue #383's retry-history diagnosis. It proves every failed attempt is recorded with typed attribution data, the first application failure wins over later transport noise in either order, all-transport failures use the final attempt, identical details preserve the legacy single-line message, divergent details are bounded, non-retryable failures remain byte-compatible, the final error log matches the raised message, and the `init_ok` readiness diagnosis still fires.
```
